name: Biliary Cystadenocarcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Biliary Cystadenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of malignant epithelial tumor arising from cystic bile duct epithelium
Imaging evidence (CT/MRI) of multiloculated cystic hepatic lesion with mural nodules or septations
Elevated serum CA 19-9 or CEA levels supportive but not definitive
Symptoms of biliary obstruction or abdominal mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings are required for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from benign biliary cystadenoma is critical and requires histopathological evaluation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable right upper quadrant abdominal mass
searchTerms: felt lump in right upper belly
abdominal swelling in right upper quadrant
jaundice worsening due to bile blockage
progressive yellow skin from bile duct obstruction
pruritus related to liver bile retention

occasional.symptomName: Fever due to secondary infection or cholangitis

searchTerms: high liver enzymes in blood tests
persistent exhaustion due to health problems

rare.symptomName: Ascites due to malignant peritoneal spread
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from cancer spread
abdominal swelling due to cancer fluid

rare.symptomName: Hepatic encephalopathy secondary to liver dysfunction
searchTerms: confusion and altered consciousness from liver disease
signs of high blood pressure in liver veins

laboratory: Cholestatic liver function test abnormalities (elevated alkaline phosphatase, GGT, bilirubin)
imaging: Multiloculated cystic hepatic lesion with internal septations and mural nodules on CT or MRI
Contrast enhancement of cyst wall and nodules
Biliary ductal dilatation proximal to lesion
genetic: No specific genetic mutations routinely identified; molecular profiling may reveal KRAS or TP53 mutations in some cases
other: Histopathology showing malignant epithelial cells with papillary or glandular structures arising from cystic bile duct epithelium

distinguishingFeatures: Benign cystic lesion without malignant histopathological features
Absence of mural nodules or solid enhancing components on imaging
Normal or mildly elevated tumor markers
Solid mass lesion rather than cystic
Typically presents with biliary strictures rather than cystic lesions

redFlags: Onset of obstructive jaundice with abdominal mass
Elevated tumor markers (CA 19-9, CEA) in cystic liver lesion
references: Zen Y, et al. Biliary cystadenocarcinoma: clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical study of 15 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2011.
Kwon CHD, et al. Imaging features of biliary cystadenocarcinoma: differentiation from biliary cystadenoma. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 2014.
